review.reviewer: Riley Morgan / scoped implementation evidence review
conditions: Prefer manifest-first when the Operational Scenario routing index exists and is current.
Use code-search-first as fallback when the index is unavailable, stale, or lacks a usable match for the task.
rationale: Both strategies passed the same validation gate under the same repository/runtime conditions.
Remote-call count was equal at two calls per strategy.
Manifest-first reduced discovery payload from 19,816 bytes to 4,037 bytes and reduced candidate ambiguity from four candidates to one declared path.
The proof supports a scoped retrieval preference only; it does not establish universal GitHub search or Tool superiority.
evidence: Live read-only comparison executed through the connected GitHub app on 2026-09-21.
Issue #187 established the compact routing manifest used by the manifest-first strategy.
PR #189 Repository validation run 35682858750 passed the comparison contract, focused tests, and full repository validation.

stale_when: Operational Scenario index schema or routing semantics materially change.
